findings.title: Cron deletes cancelled reminders before they are cancelled in SendGrid
findings.body: The existing `deleteMany` for EMAIL reminders with `scheduledDate <= now` runs first. The new cancellation query only looks at `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour` and runs after it. A reminder flagged `cancelled` whose date is within the next hour is cancelled correctly. But if the cron is late or misses a run, the reminder row is deleted without ever calling SendGrid, which loses the cancellation. The cancel query also has no `method: EMAIL` filter, so cancelled SMS rows would be sent to the SendGrid API. SMS rows are deleted directly now, so this is mostly latent.

findings.title: One SendGrid failure aborts all remaining cancellations, and unscheduled reminders are not filtered
findings.body: The loop awaits `client.request` for each reminder inside a single try/catch. If one request fails (rate limit, invalid batch id), the loop exits. The remaining cancellations are skipped and the rows already queued for deletion are never awaited. Those emails may still go out. The query also does not filter on `scheduled: true` or `referenceId != null`, so a null batch_id could be sent.

findings.title: Cancellation window is too tight for SendGrid and cron timing
findings.body: Cancelled reminders are only processed within 1 hour before send, but the cron runs every 15 minutes. Reminders cancelled later than the window allows (or after a missed run) can still be sent. SendGrid also requires cancellation of scheduled sends well ahead of the send time. In addition, `client.setApiKey` is only called in emailReminderManager, not in this file, so the cron's `client.request` calls may be unauthenticated unless that module happens to be imported.

findings.title: Reminder with null referenceId is deleted even though it may already be scheduled or unscheduled
findings.body: When `referenceId` is null the row is deleted directly. That is fine for unscheduled rows. But a row whose email was concurrently picked up by the cron (scheduled with a batch id after this read) would have its DB row deleted while the email stays scheduled. This is a race, and the caller passes a stale `referenceId`.

findings.title: Rescheduling cancels reminders with immediateDelete but the fire-and-forget promise is not awaited and the row is never removed
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` is async and is called inside `forEach` without await, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch its failures. In the immediate path it cancels in SendGrid but does not delete or mark the DB row, so a `cancelled` flag is never set. The stale reminder row remains and the cron later tries to send or cancel it again. SMS reminders are also deleted unconditionally.

findings.title: Authorization check on reminder deletion removed
findings.body: The old code deleted reminders with a `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }` condition. The new code passes only `reminder.id` to the delete helpers, dropping that ownership scoping. The reminders are selected by the user's bookings, so the practical risk is low. Separately, the diff reformats a large commented-out block (stripping indentation), which is unrelated noise.
